title: Evil twin attack
goal_html: Students practice the core analytic skill: given a raw wireless scan table (SSID, BSSID, security level, signal strength), identify which entries are suspicious and justify each flagged entry by citing a specific indicator. Ties to LO 1.3.B (identify indicators of evil-twin attacks on public Wi-Fi).
steps_html:
1. (5 min) Each pair reads the scan table silently and writes down which rows they think are suspicious, without discussing yet.
  2. (8 min) Partners compare their lists. For each disagreement, argue your case using the detection rules from atom.md: same SSID / different BSSID, or same SSID / weaker security. Agree on a final answer.
  3. (7 min) Open the simulation. Work through its scan rounds. Check whether your reasoning from the table translates, the sim uses the same analytic rules.
  4. (5 min) One partner reads from the scan table, acting as the "attacker", they explain why their evil-twin entry (row 2 or 4) would fool a casual user. The other partner explains the defensive response.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the WIDS analyst (identifies and justifies flags), the other is the attacker (argues why each evil twin is convincing to a victim). Swap roles for the second round. Both record: indicator observed, reason it is suspicious, defensive action.
exit_html: Each student submits one written sentence per suspicious row: name the row, the specific indicator (duplicate BSSID, security downgrade, etc.), and one action a user could take to avoid connecting to that AP.
